card_quote: Default disposition: 'I've heard all this before.' Enjoys catching books in errors.
how_read: Library copy, pencil in hand, keeping his own tally against the book. Reads in order over about a week, quickly through the ones he already knows, slowly where something is new or wrong. Checks the contents page numbers and the surprises list against the book because he does that with everything. Skips the certificate and the sign-up pitch.

w1_best.why: The red-dotted bomber was drawn around 2005 by a designer. I had that picture in my head as Wald's own.
I believed the Delhi cobra breeding for forty years. It traces to one 'was alleged' in Madras. That one got me.
Twenty-six blacks at Monte Carlo has no record before Huff in 1959. Nice catch.
Juran owning up to naming it wrong in 1974 is the sort of detail I like.
Potato famine as the textbook Giffen good is discredited. My economics text taught it.

w1_flat.why: Everybody has heard that this is a Vitruvius story.
A repeat of Hanlon's razor with a new name on the front.
Second page on Wald to say the first page's lesson is true after all.
A napkin nobody remembers. Disputed, who cares.
Dawkins coined meme, a TRUE I could have given at age twelve.

w1_review.headline: Decent myth-buster with sloppy production
w1_review.body: I knew roughly a third of these and I learned a dozen things, like the red-dot plane and the Delhi cobras, and I like that it names its sources and keeps the hedges. But a book of corrections should not contradict its own stamp on the Franklin page, repeat entries to pad to a hundred, or print page references that are off by several pages. The AI-drafting note on page 2 does not inspire confidence either. Bottom line: borrow it from the library, do not buy the second one until they proofread.

w2_review_first: It is a myth-quiz with a good mix of stories, and I found maybe a dozen I had wrong. But it repeats itself and the editing is sloppy, a stamp contradicting its own paragraph on one page. Get it from the library.

w2_lost.why: Second Hanlon razor page, nothing new.
Wald again, I read the heading and skipped to the Tell someone line.
Hardin part two. I was paging ahead.

w2_read_aloud.why: Nobody at the table will believe the cobras were never bred in Delhi.
Everyone has seen the red-dot bomber, nobody knows it was drawn in 2005.
Monte Carlo and 26 blacks, they will all say they have heard it.
Six downloads before the lawsuit is a good number to spring on people.
Rat tails, because it is the documented one after the cobra falls apart.

w2_cut.why: Folds into the napkin page, one entry would do.
Same Hardin essay as the one before it.
Peter Principle as satire, everyone knows.
One watch or two, a smug line and a thin answer.

w2_book2: More padding and more proofing errors, or any more trick-question framing where one story gets two pages to fool me.
